The '''Einasto profile''' (or '''Einasto model''') is a mathematical function that describes how the density <math>\rho</math> of a spherical stellar system varies with distance <math>r</math> from its center. [[Jaan Einasto]] introduced his model at a 1963 conference in [[Alma-Ata]], Kazakhstan.<ref>[[Jaan Einasto|J. Einasto]] (1965), Kinematics and dynamics of stellar systems, ''Trudy Inst. Astrofiz. Alma-Ata'' '''5''', 87</ref>

[[File:Einasto 2.jpg|thumb|300px|Einasto profiles. The order of <math>\alpha</math> is reversed for large radii.]]

The Einasto profile possesses a [[power law]] [[logarithmic scale|logarithmic]] slope of the form:
<math display="block">\gamma(r) \equiv -\frac{\operatorname{d}\ln\rho(r)}{\operatorname{d}\ln r} \propto r^{\alpha}</math>
which can be rearranged to give
<math display="block">\rho(r) \propto \exp{(-Ar^\alpha)} .</math>
The parameter <math>\alpha</math> controls the degree of curvature of the profile. This can be seen by computing the slope on a log-log plot:
<math display="block">\frac{d \ln\rho}{d \ln r} \propto -r^{\alpha} .</math>

The larger <math>\alpha</math>, the more rapidly the slope varies with radius (see figure). Einasto's law can be described as a generalization of a power law, <math>\rho\propto r^{-N}</math>, which has a constant slope on a log-log plot.

Einasto's model has the same mathematical form as [[Sersic's law]], which is used to describe the surface brightness (i.e. projected density) profile of galaxies, except that the Einasto model describes a spherically symmetric density distribution in 3 dimensions, whereas the Sersic law describes a circularly symmetric surface density distribution in two dimensions.

Einasto's model has been used to describe many types of system, including [[galaxy|galaxies]],<ref>J. Einasto and U. Haud (1989), [http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1989A%26A...223...89E  Galactic models with massive corona. I - Method. II - Galaxy] ''Astron. Astrophys.'' '''223''', 89</ref> and [[dark matter halo]]s.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Navarro|first1=Julio|authorlink1=Julio Navarro (astrophysicist)|display-authors=etal|title=The inner structure of ΛCDM haloes - III. Universality and asymptotic slopes|journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society|date=April 2004|volume=349|issue=3|pages=1039–1051|doi=10.1111/j.1365-2966.2004.07586.x|doi-access=free |arxiv=astroph/0311231|bibcode=2004MNRAS.349.1039N}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Merritt  | first1 = David | author1-link = David Merritt|author2-link=Alister W.
